title: 第3章　热切的归属与强烈的渴望：追寻伊斯坦布尔的城市权利
originalTitle: CHAPTER 3 Passionate Belongings and Intense Longings: Tracing the Right to the City in Istanbul

zh: 第3章　热切的归属与强烈的渴望：追寻伊斯坦布尔的城市权利
en: CHAPTER 3 Passionate Belongings and Intense Longings: Tracing the Right to the City in Istanbul

zh: 要对伊斯坦布尔的经验展开有意义的讨论，就必须通过这座城市独特的动力，以及它与西方进程的差异，来理解其城市化。彼得·桑德斯援引伊万·塞莱尼（1981）提醒我们，20世纪70年代进行的大量研究有一种“强烈倾向：把西方资本主义城市视为当代城市发展的范式，忽视资本主义与非资本主义社会（第三世界或东欧）之间的差异，也忽视不同西方资本主义国家中的差异”（2005，148）。同样，伊丽莎白·威尔逊强调，有必要避免一种“种族中心主义且过于简单化”的看法，它忽略了“不同第三世界国家及其城市之间的差异”（1991，122）。她补充说，“把所有第三世界城市混为一谈，也是一种非历史的做法”；例如，中东的许多城市比拉丁美洲的城市更古老，而拉美城市又比许多非洲城市更古老（122）。
en: For a meaningful discussion on the experiences in Istanbul we have to understand the city’s urbanisation through its unique dynamics and differences from Western processes. Peter Saunders, referring to Iván Szelényi (1981), reminds us of the “strong tendency in much of the work conducted through the 1970s to take western capitalist cities as the paradigm of contemporary urbanism, and to ignore variations both between capitalist and non-capitalist (Third World or eastern European) societies, and within different western capitalist countries” (2005, 148). Similarly, Elizabeth Wilson underscores the need for refraining from an “ethnocentric and oversimplified” view, ignoring “the differences among various third-world countries and their cities” (1991, 122). She adds that “it is also ahistorical to lump all third-world cities together”, as many cities of the Middle East for instance are older than Latin American cities which are older than many African cities (122).

zh: 阿利米娅等人在针对北非与中东若干穆斯林城市的研究中强调，他们寻求“一种理解城市性的多学科视角”，避免把城市性理解为“单纯的量化指标”（2018，3）。他们指出，“是否存在一种普遍的城市性模式，是值得怀疑的”，并试图回答“为什么似乎存在多种随时间与空间而变化的城市性类型”（3）。桑德斯似乎为这一问题提供了答案。他解释说，“随着不同利益群体努力使自身的价值与抱负获得表达，城市生活的含义也会因时间与地点而异”；由此他断言，“因此，不可能存在一个概括一切的城市生活概念”（2005，148）。
en: In their research based in selected North African and Middle Eastern Muslim cities, Alimia et al. emphasise that they search for “a multidisciplinary perspective of understanding urbanity” that refrains from understanding it “as a simple measure of metrics” (2018, 3). They point out that “it is doubtful if there exists one universal model of urbanity” and try to answer “why there appear to be multiple types of urbanities that vary over time and space” (3). Saunders seems to have an answer to that question as he explains that “the meaning of urbanism will differ over different times and places as different interests struggle to realize the expression of their own values and aspirations” and concludes that “there can thus be no generic concept of urbanism” (2005, 148).

zh: 同样，萨斯基娅·萨森认为，“城市性”（urbanity）一词“承载着西方的世界主义观念，规定了公共空间是什么或应当是什么”（2005，1）。她指出，“有一些城市性类型，并不符合西方发展出来的这套极为庞大的城市论述”（1）。她以上海为例：人们晚间聚在一起打牌。她据此提出，“我们从西欧语境中发展出来的公共空间观念，未必能帮助我们以十分有用的方式解读上海这样的城市，甚至也未必能用于墨西哥城”（1）。萨森提出用“城市特质”（cityness）替代“城市性”（urbanity），以便“辨认那些可能以极为不同的方式构成的城市性”（1）。她希望形成一种概念化方式，使“在西方人看来可能是城市蔓延”的现象等种种可能性，都能够在不“局限于某些城市形态”的情况下得到考察，因为“还存在更多的可能性”（2）。
en: Similarly, Saskia Sassen argues that the term “urbanity” is “charged with a Western sense of cosmopolitanism of what public space is or should be” (2005, 1). She acknowledges that “there are kinds of urbanity that do not fit with this very large body of urbanism developed in the West” (1). She gives the example of Shanghai, where people gather together in the evenings to play cards, and contends that “the notion of public space as we have developed it out of a Western European context might not help us read a city such as Shanghai, or perhaps even Mexico City, in ways that are very useful” (1). Sassen offers the term “cityness” instead of “urbanity” in order to “detect urbanities that may be constituted in very different ways” (1). She aims to arrive at a conceptualisation where possibilities such as “what to the Western eye might look like urban sprawl” could be examined in a way not “limited to, certain urban forms”, since “there are more possibilities” (2).

zh: 伊斯坦布尔的复杂阶段
en: Istanbul’s Complex Phases

zh: 众所周知，“第三世界的城市化并没有像西方国家那样，伴随着相应的经济繁荣”（Hay 1986，72）。因此，正如威尔逊所指出的，为了对第三世界城市作出有意义的分析，我们必须克服这样一种“潜在预设：城市化必然始终遵循同一条道路——即西方城市在工业化时期历史地走过的那条道路”（1991，122）。
en: It is a well-known fact that “urbanization in the Third World has not been accompanied by concomitant economic prosperity as it was in western nations” (Hay 1986, 72). Therefore, as Wilson points out, we have to overcome “the underlying presumption that urbanisation must always follow the same path – that taken historically by western cities in the industrial period” (1991, 122) for a meaningful analysis of third-world cities.

zh: 1976年，时任威斯康星大学中东研究项目主任的土耳其学者凯末尔·卡尔帕特，根据在伊斯坦布尔三个棚户区开展的大量田野调查，写出了一部研究该市棚户住房的奠基性著作。在这部著作中，卡尔帕特参照中东、非洲与拉丁美洲的经验，从与其他第三世界城市比较的视角，对伊斯坦布尔的城市化作出了深入分析。他的框架与解释成功避开了以西方为中心的狭隘城市化观所具有的缺陷。
en: In 1976, Turkish scholar Kemal Karpat, chair of the Middle East Studies Program at the University of Wisconsin at the time, wrote a seminal book on shanty housing in Istanbul, based on extensive fieldwork in three shanty towns in the city. In this work, Karpat makes an in-depth analysis of Istanbul’s urbanisation in comparative perspective with other third-world cities, with references to Middle Eastern, African and Latin American experiences. His framework and explanations successfully refrain from the shortcomings of a narrow view of urbanisation based on Western-centrism.

zh: 卡尔帕特强调，“第三世界的传统城市，尤其是穆斯林城市，与马克斯·韦伯所说的‘理想’西方城市几乎没有共同之处。它的政治与经济生活不同于乡村，但文化与宗教生活却并无不同”（2009，31）。他解释说，穆斯林城市的规划者意在提供“使乌玛（真主的共同体）臻于完满德性所必需的物质与道德条件”（31）。卡尔帕特接着强调，到了19世纪，以手工业生产为基础的穆斯林城市，在面对“西方以工业和市场为导向的经济所产生的政治与经济影响”时，已无法维系（32）。不过，他补充说，在这一形势下，中东与北非的多个穆斯林城市利用自己位于贸易路线上的地理位置，获得了城市增长的机会（32）。结果，“伊斯兰国家中一种新的村庄与城市的二分”出现了，其基础是“经济利益优先：经济利益不再被视为文化—宗教体系的一部分，而被严格地理解为市场关系”（32）。卡尔帕特认为，由此“村庄与城市之间旧有的文化与社会和谐被打破了”，这些城市，无论属于穆斯林还是非穆斯林的第三世界，最终都呈现出相似的特征（32）。“这些城市不是制造业中心，没有工业、高科技、通讯设施与固定资本，也无法为专门教育和科学研究提供施展的空间；与西方城市相比，它们不是创新中心，也不是技能高度集中的中心”（32）。
en: Karpat stresses that “the traditional city in the third world, especially the Muslim, had little in common with the ‘ideal’ Western city of Max Weber. Its political and economic life was different from that of the countryside, although its cultural and religious life was not” (2009, 31). He explains that the planners of the Muslim cities aimed at presenting “the material and moral conditions necessary for the

(community of God) to attain perfect virtue” (31). Karpat goes on by underscoring that in the nineteenth century, with its craft production, the Muslim city could not survive in the face of “the political and economic influence of the industrial, market-oriented economics of the West” (32). However, he adds that at this conjuncture various Muslim Middle Eastern and North African cities had an opportunity for urban growth, making use of their geographical location on trade routes (32). As a result of this, “a new dichotomy between village and city in the Islamic countries” emerged based on the “priority to economic interests conceived not as part of a cultural-religious system, but strictly as market relations” (32). Karpat asserts that consequently “the old cultural and social harmony between village and city was broken”, and these cities, either in the Muslim or non-Muslim third world, ultimately acquired similar characteristics (32). “These cities were not manufacturing centers, did not possess industry and high technology, communication, and fixed capital, and could not provide outlets for specialized education and scientific investigation; in comparison with Western cities, they were not centers of innovation and of high concentration of skills” (32).

zh: 卡尔帕特解释说，第二次世界大战以后，随着政治与经济的发展，这些城市开始引入“与工业发达国家相关联的技术、文化及科学特征”（32）。因此，“第三世界的‘城市’被迫沿着自身特殊的演化道路，最终通过获得某些技术，成为一种新的或现代的城市”（32）。由此，这些第三世界城市从“首位型、寄生型和正生型城市”，转变为“生成型和异生型城市——也就是现代的多功能城市”（33）。
en: Karpat explains that after World War II, as a result of political and economic developments, these cities started to bring in “the technological and the cultural and scientific features associated with industrially advanced countries” (32). Thus, “the third world ‘city’ was compelled to become a new or a modern city by following a special evolutionary path of its own, and eventually by acquiring some technology” (32). As a result of this, these third-world cities changed from being “the primate and parasitic and orthogenetic cities” to “generative and heterogenic cities – that is, the modern multifunctional cities” (33).

zh: 厄兹居尔·奥尔汉加齐指出，在19世纪奥斯曼时代，工业化十分有限；这种状况在1923年建立的土耳其共和国时期开始改变。他强调，在20世纪50至60年代乡城迁移的高峰期，土耳其多个城市，尤其是伊斯坦布尔，工业化发展迅速（私人交流，2020年5月14日）。卡尔帕特将“乡村迁移与城市化，以及二者的副产品——迁入者聚居区，或称棚户聚居区”，描述为土耳其“现代化”的内在组成部分（2009，7）。坦瑟·申亚珀勒对这一进程的概括值得长引如下：
en: Özgür Orhangazi acknowledges that, while in the 19th-century Ottoman era industrialisation was very limited, this began changing in the Turkish Republic, which was established in 1923. He emphasises that at the height of the rural–urban migration in the 1950s and the 1960s industrialisation was rapid in various cities of the country, particularly in Istanbul (pers. comm., 14 May 2020). Karpat describes “rural migration and urbanization and their by-product – the migrant, or squatter, settlements” as the intrinsic components of Turkey’s “modernization” (2009, 7). Tansı Şenyapılı’s summary of this process is worth quoting at length:

zh: 20世纪50年代，一场规模空前的迁移冲击了城市，迁入者主要是缺乏技能、不识字的原乡村居民。然而，在那个时期，无论投资、工业还是服务业，都尚未得到充分发展。因此，城市的经济空间还没有准备好接纳和雇用他们。临近1955年，在通货膨胀的经济政策影响下，加上对展示门面式城市投资的重视，边缘部门渐渐出现了面向棚户区（gecekondu）劳动力的就业机会，服务业也为受过教育的中产阶级女性提供了工作。（1981a，207）
en: In the fifties, a migration of unprecedented volume consisting mainly of unskilled, illiterate, former villagers hit the cities. Yet, in that period, neither the investments nor the industry nor the service sectors were sufficiently developed. Therefore, urban economic space was not ready to accept and employ them. Slowly towards 1955, under the influence of inflationary economic policies and emphasis on show-case type urban investments, employment opportunities appeared in the marginal sector for gecekondu [shanty] labour and jobs opened in the service sector for educated middle class women. (1981a, 207)

zh: 在这样的城市条件下，乡村迁入者的身份成为一个被广泛讨论的问题。下文主要参照凯末尔·卡尔帕特与缪贝杰尔·克赖的著作来分析这些讨论；他们是20世纪70年代土耳其两位重要的社会学家，都对迁移问题有大量论述。
en: Under such conditions in the city, the status of the rural migrant became a widely discussed topic. Below, these discussions are analysed with references mainly to Kemal Karpat and Mübeccel Kıray, two leading sociologists of Turkey in the 1970s who wrote extensively on migration.

zh: 城市化，还是伪城市化？
en: Urbanisation or Pseudo-Urbanisation?

zh: 缪贝杰尔·克赖在1972年撰写的一篇文章中断言，“住在棚屋里的人，无论如何都不再是农民了”（2007b，98）。但是，她补充说，由于这个国家的工业化十分缓慢，组织化进程比工业化还要缓慢，“这批不得不离开土地的人口，没有机会获得一种工业—城市身份，只能从事零散、微小、非生产性的服务工作”（98）。她强调，“像样的工业岗位”数量有限；然而，“这些人没有一个从事农业生产，所以他们已经不再是‘农民’”（98）。她建议使用“伪城市化”和“伪城市居民”这两个概念，因为“城市中经济生产与职业所涉及的关系如此不定型，而这种不定型状态又延续了如此之久，以至于棚屋与手艺行业已经成为城市生活的重要方面”（99）。
en: Mübeccel Kıray, in an article she wrote in 1972, asserts that “people living in shanties are by no means peasants any longer” (2007b, 98). Yet, she adds, since the country industrialised very slowly, and became organised even more slowly than that, “this population which had to leave its land behind do not find the chance to gain an industrial-urban identity, and work in random, small, non-producing service works” (98). She emphasises that the number of “plausible industrial jobs” is limited; however “none of these people work in agricultural production, so they are no longer ‘peasants’” (98). She recommends the use of “pseudo-urbanisation and pseudo-urbanite” since “relationships involved in economic production and the vocations in the city are so amorphous, and this amorphousness has been ongoing for so long, that the shanties and craftsmanship have become an important aspect of urban life” (99).

zh: 对于为强调第三世界城市化未伴随工业化而提出的“城市农民”和“伪城市化”等概念，卡尔帕特告诫我们，不要用“精英主义的或西方的城市观念”来评判第三世界城市（2009，20）。他承认这些第三世界城市存在“过度拥挤和经济发展不足”，但认为，与村庄中的生活相比，这里的生活水平仍然较高（2009，20）。针对土耳其的情形，坦瑟·申亚珀勒作了如下解释：“男人劳动得少一些，女人一般不劳动，孩子则享有教育与其他城市服务”（1981a，213）。

While acknowledging “overcrowding and insufficient economic development” in these third-world cities, Karpat contends that the standard of living in them is high compared with life back in the villages (2009, 20). For the Turkish context, Tansı Şenyapılı explains this as follows: “men work less, women in general do not work, children benefit from education and other urban services” (1981a, 213).

zh: 此外，正如奥尔汉加齐所解释的，就伊斯坦布尔而言，20世纪50年代起，城市确实经历了工业化，但工业岗位的数量不足以满足大量迁入者的就业需要（私人交流，2020年5月14日）。卡尔帕特解释说，在土耳其，无法在城市“新建立的工业”中找到工作的迁入者，要么进入服务业，或进入依靠廉价劳动力运转的“第二（工业）部门”，要么通过沿街叫卖谋生（2009，22）。他补充说，第三世界城市存在对“无技能、低工资工人”的需求，乡村迁入者为小企业提供了廉价劳动力来源（22）。

Karpat explains that in Turkey migrants who could not find employment in “the newly established industries” in the cities either worked in the service sector or “secondary (industrial) sector” which functioned on inexpensive labour; or else they made their income as street vendors (2009, 22). He adds that in third-world cities there was a need for “unskilled and low-paid workers” and rural migrants served as a source of inexpensive labour to small enterprises (22).

zh: 正如卡尔帕特指出的，推动乡城迁移的动机并不限于更高的收入和生活水平；其中还存在“一种对城市的文化与历史认同感”（27）。卡尔帕特观察到，第三世界国家的居民将城市看作“一种更优越的存在形式”，并补充说：“城市生活——şehir、madina、polis，或urbanismo——所被赋予的崇高地位，是亚洲、非洲与拉丁美洲文化中一个根深蒂固的要素。在穆斯林文化中，madaniyyat——即文明——一词源于madina，也就是城市”（244，注47）。

zh: 卡尔帕特将土耳其的大规模乡城迁移描述为“根本性、持久性结构变迁”的结果，它有别于暂时性的迁移浪潮（33）。土耳其结构变迁的乡村维度，并不限于农业机械化；在迁移发生的不同年代，乡村中会出现不同的动力（Yıldırmaz 2017，71—99）。西南·耶尔德尔马兹认为，城市研究著作普遍忽略了这一事实，因为“研究者不关注乡村发生了什么，而主要把注意力集中在城市的发展与转型上”（98）。
en: Karpat describes the mass rural–urban migration in Turkey as the outcome of “basic permanent structural changes” unlike temporary migration waves (33). The rural dimension of Turkey’s structural changes was not limited to the mechanisation of farming, as various dynamics in the countryside emerged at different decades of migration (Yıldırmaz 2017, 71–99). According to Sinan Yıldırmaz, overlooking this fact is common in the works of urban studies as “researchers do not pay attention to what happens in the countryside, but focus mainly on the developments and the transformation in the city” (98).

zh: 卡尔帕特解释说，如果这个国家的结构变迁不是持久性的，而只是一种暂时情况，那么“城市［伊斯坦布尔］或许能够把新来者吸纳进自身既有的结构和僵硬的城市文化之中，从而将他们同化”（2009，33）。卡尔帕特以“僵硬的城市文化”如此准确地描述的现象，正处于导论中所讨论的伊斯坦布尔人与非伊斯坦布尔人之分的核心。
en: Karpat explains that if the structural changes in the country were not permanent, but a temporary case, then “the city [Istanbul] might have assimilated the newcomers by absorbing them into its prevailing structure and rigid urban culture” (2009, 33). The phenomenon described perfectly by Karpat as “rigid urban culture” is at the core of the Istanbulite versus non-Istanbulite divide discussed in the introductory chapter.

zh: 在解释了历史动力，以及由此带来的经济与结构变迁之后，卡尔帕特将穆斯林国家的第三世界城市概括为主要“在一定程度上兼具传统伊斯兰城市与欧洲城市的特征，同时又包含乡村的民俗文化、共同体情感、自然态度、实用主义与物质主义”（33）。他补充说，当居住在棚户聚居区的大量乡村迁入者加入城市人口时，多数中东穆斯林城市发生了显著变化，“失去了传统的精英主义特征”（34）。他提醒我们，这是一个双向过程。在指出“乡村迁移对第三世界城市化所起的作用”的同时，卡尔帕特也强调“城市对迁入者的改造性影响”（34）。正如萨森所观察到的，“城市生活的日常动力及其相互依赖关系，促成了一种城市主体的形成，它不同于族群主体、宗教主体或种族化主体”（2017，35）。这个城市主体，与刚刚来到城市时的乡村迁入者，已是大不相同的人。“城市对迁入者具有深刻的改变作用，尤其体现在职业习惯、社会和政治行动的组织形式、家庭规模与关系、抱负水平，以及与交流相关的价值观方面”（Karpat 2009，34）。卡尔帕特进一步强调，“这种变化之所以发生，很大程度上是因为城市本身也正在被工业化、技术与政治行动所改变。对于城市，这种情况可以被描述为‘现代化’；对于乡村迁入者，则可以被描述为‘城市化’”（34）。在伊斯坦布尔，既有精英群体强烈抵制将迁入者接纳为城市的新成员，尽管他们是城市现代化进程中不可避免的组成部分。正如卡尔帕特指出的，“新来者把自己对社会和世界的看法强加给了城市，这往往令老城里人既愤怒又沮丧”（2009，32）。随着棚屋在伊斯坦布尔蔓延，住在其中的乡村迁入者被这些既有居民轻蔑地视为城里的农民。
en: After explaining the historical dynamics, and economic and structural changes thereof, Karpat describes the third-world cities in Muslim countries as predominantly “compris[ing] to a degree both the features of the traditional Islamic and European cities, along with the folk culture, community feeling, natural attitudes, pragmatism, and materialism of the countryside” (33). He adds that when a massive number of rural migrants dwelling in squatter settlements joined the urban population, most of the Middle Eastern Muslim cities changed significantly, “losing their traditional elitist features” (34). He reminds us that this is a two-way process. While acknowledging “the role played by rural migration on urbanization in the third world” Karpat draws attention to the “transforming impact of the city on the migrant” (34). As Sassen observes, “the daily dynamics and interdependencies of life in the city contribute to the making of an urban subject, as distinct from an ethnic, religious, or racialized subject” (2017, 35). This urban subject is a highly different person from the rural migrant at the stage of his/her arrival at the city. “The city has a profound changing effect on the migrant, especially in occupational habits, organizations for social and political actions, family size and relations, levels of aspiration, and values related to communication” (Karpat 2009, 34). Karpat further stresses that “this change occurs in large measure because the city itself is being transformed by industrialization, technology, and political action. This situation can be described as ‘modernization’ for the city and ‘urbanization’ for the rural migrant” (34). In the case of Istanbul, the elite establishment was highly resistant to accepting migrants as new members of the city who are an inevitable element of its modernisation process. As Karpat acknowledges, “the newcomers have imposed on the city their own outlook on society and the world, often to the outraged dismay of old urbanites” (2009, 32). As shanties spread in Istanbul, rural migrants living in them were scorned as peasants in the city by these established members.

zh: 多种城市性
en: Multiple Urbanities

zh: 正如萨森所观察到的，“在城市中，我们可以看到新主体与新身份的生成，而在乡村地区或一个国家整体层面上，这种生成或许是不可能的”（2013，214）。城市经验本身具有改变其居民的潜能，城中的迁入者通过不同的适应阶段，成为一个新的人。“迁入者与棚户居民融入城市——换言之，他们的城市化”（Karpat 2009，230）是一个被广泛讨论的问题；而正如博·格伦隆德指出的，谁算是城市居民，是一个“过于模糊、过于复杂”（2007，112-02）的问题，无法用一个简单的答案加以回应。坦瑟·申亚珀勒根据迁入者非正规的就业和住房策略，将他们描述为边缘人口。她认为，他们“在文化与社会关系方面并未融入”，但却成功成为“经济与物质空间［……］的一部分”，其中“运用了理性的解决办法”（1978，44）。Wenfei Wang与Cindy Fan在研究中国乡村迁入者融入问题的文章中，将融入划分为三类：“经济融入”“社会／文化融入”和“身份认同融入”（2012，733）。T.申亚珀勒在上述引文中所指出的是，在她写作时，伊斯坦布尔的迁入者尚未在社会、文化或身份认同方面融入；但在寻找经济生存之道、创造栖身之所方面，他们凭借非正规的解决办法维持着自己的生活。
en: As Sassen observes, “in cities we can see the making of new subjects and identities that would not be possible in, for example, rural areas or a country at large” (2013, 214). With the inherent potential of the urban experience to transform its inhabitants, the migrant in the city becomes a new person through various stages of adaptation. “The integration of migrants and squatters into city – in other words, their urbanization” (Karpat 2009, 230) is an issue widely discussed; and as Bo Grönlund points out, who is an urbanite is “too vague and too complex” (2007, 112-02) an issue to have a simple answer. Based on migrants’ informal employment and housing strategies, Tansı Şenyapılı describes them as a marginal population. She argues that they “are not integrated in terms of cultural and social relations” but that they succeed in being part of the “economic and physical space [...] making use of rational solutions” (1978, 44). Wenfei Wang and Cindy Fan, in their article about the integration of rural migrants in China, divide integration into three categories: “economic integration”, “social/cultural integration” and “identity integration” (2012, 733). What T. Şenyapılı points out in the above quotation is that migrants in Istanbul, at the time she writes, are not integrated socially or culturally or in terms of identity; while in terms of finding ways to survive economically, and of creating a place to live, they manage their lives through their informal solutions.

zh: 一种被广泛接受的观点认为，那些使迁入者得以在城市环境中生存下来的策略，并不能让他们在文化和社会方面融入。按照这一观点，这又使得身份认同层面的融入不可能实现。T.申亚珀勒强调，从事一份被认为属于城市的工作，并不足以实现融入；迁入者还需要“足以［……］参与城市生活的收入”（1978，38）。厄恩代尔·申亚珀勒将经济困难描述为适应城市生活的一道障碍（1981b，101）。在他看来，“农民迁入城市时，因为他们的劳动变成了城市劳动，而且住在城市里，所以被接纳为‘城市居民’；但是，他们并不是真正意义上的‘城市居民’”，他将其描述为“正在城市化的农民”（128）。他补充说，如果“城市中的城市性活动（或非农业活动）”，以及那些“稳定、健康、能够带来足够收入”的工作有所增加，那么这一城市化进程也将获得更大的动力（128）。
en: It is a widely accepted argument that the strategies which allow migrants to survive in the urban environment do not enable them to culturally and socially integrate. This brings the impossibility of integration in terms of identity, according to this view. T. Şenyapılı stresses that working in a job which is accepted as urban is not sufficient for integration, the migrant also needs “income that [...] is sufficient to participate in urban life” (1978, 38). Önder Şenyapılı describes economic hardship as a barrier to adaptation to life in the urban context (1981b, 101). According to him “when peasants move to the city they are accepted as ‘urbanites’ since their labour becomes urban and they live in the city but, they are not ‘urbanites’ in the real sense”, and he describes them as “urbanizing peasants” (128). He adds that if “urban activities (or non-agricultural activities) in the city” and jobs that are “consistent, healthy, and bringing sufficient income” increase, then this process of urbanisation will also gain momentum (128).

zh: 卡尔帕特将迁入者的城市化描述为“个体与集体在社会政治和心理层面的特定文化适应过程”（2009，137），他对融入抱有更为乐观的看法。在他看来，尽管城中的迁入者保留了“村庄文化与组织方式”，但“迁入者仍会使自己适应城市条件，并逐渐改变自身物质生活的面貌与文化观念”（138）。卡尔帕特如此概括这一过程：“城市化一词，既包含迁入者通过职业变化，以及逐渐接受城市生活的物质与文化方面而实现的‘融入’，也包含城市对民俗文化某些要素的吸纳”（138）。根据1968年在伊斯坦布尔三个棚户区进行的田野调查，卡尔帕特指出，迁入者有兴趣“与城市接触，并希望了解城中的居民”，这是“其城市化的重要组成部分”（150）。“然而，城市的既有居民并未表现出明显的愿望，要去了解棚户居民［居住在棚屋中的迁入者］并与之融合”（155）。他补充说，即使那些承认经济与社会原因使迁移不可避免的既有居民，也并未停止使用敌视迁入者的话语；他们认为迁入者对城市氛围产生了负面影响（155）。
en: Karpat, who describes the urbanisation of migrants as “specific processes of individual and collective sociopolitical and psychological acculturation” (2009, 137), has a more optimistic perception of integration. According to him, while “the village culture and modes of organization” are protected by migrants in the city, “the migrant adapts himself to urban conditions and gradually changes his physical living and cultural outlook” (138). Karpat summarises this process as follows: “the term

encompasses both the migrant’s ‘integration’ through occupational change and gradual adoption of physical and cultural aspects of urban life and the city’s adoption of some elements of folk culture” (138). Based on the fieldwork conducted in three shanty towns of Istanbul in 1968, Karpat draws attention to migrants’ interest in “contact with the city and desire to know its inhabitants” as “a significant part in their urbanization” (150). “The established city population, however, showed no apparent desire to know, and integrate with the squatters [migrants living in shanties]” (155). He adds that even those members of the established population who accepted the inevitability of migration due to economic and social reasons did not refrain from a hostile discourse against migrants whom they viewed as a negative impact on the urban atmosphere (155).

zh: 在被同化之前，迁入者在这个陌生、艰难、有时甚至充满敌意的城市环境中，始终面临着异化的风险。卡尔帕特认为，“经济与职业融入”的过程“是对边缘性的回应”，而“同化［……］则是医治异化的一种办法”（43）。在这样的语境中，棚户区对迁入者的意义远远超出了一个普通街区；正如卡尔帕特准确地观察到的，它成为城市中的“一块‘乡村’飞地”（36）。“共同体生活为棚户居民提供了一种心理上的安全感与归属感，以及群体认同；这也构成了他接受共同体至上地位的理由”（128）。他援引安德烈·西米奇（1973）的观察：“迁入者的异化问题，通过继续参与以村庄为基础的亲属网络而得到平衡；与此同时，新的联系也逐渐在城市共同体中建立起来”（转引自Karpat 2009，246，注69）。正如这段引文所阐明的，城市中的新联系与新网络，并非一夜之间便能出现，而是随着时间一步一步形成的。换言之，融入是一个长期过程。因此，对迁入者来说，共同体所提供的支持机制至关重要，使他们在充满挑战的适应过程中不至于迷失方向、丧失自身的完整性。卡尔帕特总结说，“对共同体文化的依恋、由此产生的归属感，以及通过所有权获得的安全感，防止了棚户居民的心理瓦解与异化，并间接促进了他们融入城市环境”（232）。
en: Until the migrant is assimilated she/he is faced with the risk of alienation in this unfamiliar, difficult and sometimes hostile environment of the city. Karpat contends that while the “economic and occupational integration” process “is the response to
[...] is one remedy for

” (43). Within such a context, for the migrant, the shanty town acquires a meaning much more than simply a neighbourhood; as Karpat aptly observes, it becomes “a ‘rural’ enclave in the city” (36). “The communal life provides the squatter with a sense of psychological security and belongingness, as well as group identity, which is his rationale for accepting the supremacy of the community” (128). He refers to Andrei Simić (1973) who observes that “problems of alienation on the part of the migrant are balanced by continuing participation as part of a village-based kinship network, while new ties are gradually created in the urban community” (quoted in Karpat 2009, 246 n. 69). As the quote elucidates, new connections and networks in the city do not emerge overnight, but over time, step by step. In other words, integration is a long-term process. That is why, for the migrant, the support mechanisms that the community offers are of crucial importance in order not to lose direction and integrity during the challenging task of adaptation. Karpat concludes that “the attachment to the communal culture, the sense of belongingness stemming from it, and the security achieved through ownership, prevent the squatters’ psychological disintegration and alienation, and indirectly facilitate their integration into the urban environment” (232).

zh: 在城市环境中，缺乏团结网络所造成的异化，可能导向虚无主义。例如，马尔科姆·詹姆斯指出，在东伦敦外围地区，“由于缺乏有关工人阶级团结或世界主义团结的替代性叙事”，出现了“种族化的、具有地域性的虚无主义行为，既表现于虚拟空间，也表现于现实空间”（2015，712）。土耳其的情形则并非如此。正如上文所述，棚户区中存在着某种世界主义式的团结。克赖指出，多项社会学研究表明，在土耳其的迁入者共同体中，“并未出现异化与失范”（1982，173—174）。这种使城市性能够拥有多种形态的复杂结构，也充当着抵御异化、失范与虚无主义的堤防。
en: Alienation due to the absence of solidarity networks can lead to nihilism in the urban setting. Malcolm James, for instance, brings attention to the “racialized and territorial acts of nihilism, in their virtual and physical manifestations” in outer East London in “the absence of alternative narratives of working-class or cosmopolitan solidarity” (2015, 712). This was not the case in the Turkish context. As explained above, there was a certain cosmopolitan solidarity in the shanty towns. As Kıray acknowledges, various sociological research demonstrates that “alienation and anomie did not emerge” in the migrant communities of Turkey (1982, 173–174). The complex structure that renders multiple versions of urbanity possible also functions as a revetment against alienation, anomie and nihilism.

zh: 在这里，简要谈谈阿拉贝斯克（arabesk，亦作arabesque）或许有所帮助；这是一种流行于棚户区的音乐风格与亚文化。在音乐上，它被视为民间音乐的一种退化形式（Stokes 1992，92）。人们认为它形态不定，受阿拉伯影响，因此将其称为arabesque；其歌词则因宿命论倾向而受到批评。马丁·斯托克斯解释说，“将阿拉贝斯克与棚户区（gecekondu）联系起来，也就把这种音乐与城市流氓无产阶级的形象联系起来：他们在劳动迁移过程中发生了错位与异化”（108）。他补充说，这种音乐被理解为“来自土耳其城市社会边缘的一则异化讯息”（120）。然而，在阿拉贝斯克中，“迁移、东南地区与棚户区（gecekondu）的语言，提供了一种表达方式，使人们能够借此辨认和呈现自身生活中的问题、困难与挫折”（132）。

同样，梅拉尔·厄兹贝克也批评将阿拉贝斯克等同于异化的倾向（2002，20—21）。厄兹贝克指出，从20世纪60年代到80年代末，这种音乐经历了不同阶段（23）。她解释说，“20世纪60年代的阿拉贝斯克音乐，并不是乡村迁入者在城市中‘与环境不相协调’的表现；恰恰相反，它成功地表现了他们与环境的协调，表现了他们寻找生存出路的方式”（27）。斯托克斯指出，阿拉贝斯克早期具有两个核心主题：“乡城迁移，以及一种跨越‘纵向’地域身份的阶级意识”（126）。斯托克斯强调，阿拉贝斯克是“一种属于城市、也为了城市的音乐”（1992，1）。
en: It might be useful to briefly mention arabesk (arabesque) at this point, a musical style and subculture which was popular in shanty towns. Musically, it was regarded as a degenerate form of folk music (Stokes 1992, 92). It was seen as amorphous with Arab influences, hence the name arabesque, and its lyrics were criticised for being fatalistic. As Martin Stokes explains, “association of arabesk with the

links the music with an image of an urban lumpen proletariat dislocated and alienated through the process of labour migration” (108). He adds that this music was received as “a message of alienation from the periphery of Turkish urban society” (120). However, in arabesk “the language of migration, the south-east, and the
provides an idiom in which people are able to identify and present problems, difficulties, and frustrations in their own existence” (132).

Similarly, Meral Özbek criticises the tendency to identify arabesk with alienation (2002, 20–21). Özbek, noting that from the 1960s until the end of the 1980s this music went through various stages (23), explains that “arabesk music in the 1960s was not a manifestation of ‘incongruity with the environment’ of rural migrants in the cities, on the contrary it was a successful manifestation of their compatibility with the environment, their way of finding a way to survive” (27). Stokes identifies two central tenets in the early phase of arabesk: “rural-urban migration and a class awareness which cut across ‘vertical’, regional identities” (126). Stokes stresses that arabesk was “a music of the city and for the city” (1992, 1).

zh: 安纳托利亚的传统民间音乐，是乡村迁入者带到城市的口头文化的一个核心组成部分；无论在阿拉贝斯克的鼎盛时期还是此后，它始终深受迁入者喜爱。民间音乐也不可避免地受到迁移现象的影响。阿斯勒·卡伊汉将20世纪70年代描述为“从传统吟游诗人过渡到关怀社会的现代诗人歌手的时期”，并将其认定为“实际上是大规模迁移的自然结果”（2014，157）。她总结说：“如今，叙述已在城市定居的安纳托利亚人命运的任务，落到了吟游诗人身上，而他们自己也参与着同一个故事”（157）。
en: Traditional folk music of Anatolia, a central component of oral culture which the rural migrants brought with them to the city, was always popular among migrants, during and after the heyday of arabesk. Inevitably, folk music was also influenced by the migration phenomenon. Aslı Kayhan describes the 1970s as “the period of transition from the traditional bard to the socially concerned modern poet-singer” and identifies it as “in effect a natural consequence of mass migration” (2014, 157). She concludes that “the task of narrating the destiny of the Anatolian person now settled in the city lies with the bards, who themselves partake of that same story” (157).

zh: 如前所述，反迁入者的话语与伊斯坦布尔人的势利心态，以及对世界主义往昔的怀旧，彼此交织。如果这种心态被一种对“伊斯坦布尔始终是一座迁移之城”的强调所取代，那么迁入者就能够与这座城市建立更牢固的依恋。这样，城市居民与乡村迁入者之间的二分便会消解，我们会将城市人口理解为由城市居民和正在成为城市居民的人组成；后者即处于城市化进程不同阶段的迁入者。不过，这种城市性概念应当是灵活的，而非僵硬的。当迁入者完成融入时，他们的城市性很可能包含其民俗文化中的要素。超越精英主义，以及僵硬、规范性的城市性理解，意味着把这些要素视为城市多样性带来的丰富性并予以接纳。这种包容性的取向，将会欢迎其他形态的城市性。
en: As discussed earlier, the anti-migrant discourse was intertwined with Istanbulite snobbism and nostalgia for a cosmopolitan past. If this mentality were replaced with an emphasis on the fact that Istanbul had always been a place of migration, then migrants could develop a stronger attachment to the city. Then, the dichotomy between urbanites and rural migrants would dissolve and we would perceive the urban population as comprising of urbanites and those who are becoming urbanites (i.e., migrants at different stages of their urbanisation process). Yet, this concept of urbanity should be flexible and not rigid. When migrants’ integration is complete, their urbanity will most probably include elements of their folk culture. Surpassing elitism and a rigid, normative understanding of urbanity means embracing these elements as the richness offered by the diversity in the city. Such an inclusive approach would welcome alternative urbanities.

zh: 在结束这一论述之前，再次参照卡尔帕特或许会有所帮助；他将土耳其乡村迁入者的城市化分为四个阶段。“第一阶段的标志，是采用城市服饰和一些城市习惯，为接受城市的观点与态度作准备”（2009，139）。卡尔帕特强调，由于女性迁入者与城市环境的接触较少，她们改变衣着所需的时间比男性更长（139）。在第二阶段，迁入者开始使用现有的“城市设施，如自来水、电力和交通，也开始定期到商店购买食物与衣服”（139）。在第三阶段，他或她倾向于“与其他城市居民建立关系”，其基础是“一种新的自我形象，以他认为更优越或更理想的城市形式为范本”（139）。卡尔帕特观察到，在城市化进程的最后阶段，迁入者达到“对城市的完全认同”，此时感到“自己不属于村庄，而属于城市”（140）。
en: Before closing this argument, it might be useful to refer to Karpat once again, who identifies four stages in the urbanisation of the rural migrant in Turkey. “The first phase is marked by the adoption of urban dress and some urban habits as preparatory steps toward assuming city views and attitudes” (2009, 139). Karpat stresses that the change in clothes takes a longer time in women migrants than in men due to their limited contact with the urban environment (139). In the second stage, the migrant starts using the available “city facilities [such] as water, electricity, and transportation, and also of regularly buying his food and clothing in shops” (139). In the third phase, he/she tends “to establish relations with other city people” based on the “new self-image modelled on urban forms that he considers superior or ideal” (139). Karpat observes that in the final stage of the urbanisation process the migrant reaches “full-identification with the city” now feeling that “he does not belong to the village but to the city” (140).

zh: 迁入者如何在城市中成为城市居民，是本书所选七部小说的一个重要主题，以下各章的分析将对此加以展示。“迁入者传统文化的变化，似乎不是以突然与过去决裂的方式发生的，而是缓慢地吸收城市影响，同时使民俗文化与之相适应”（40）。与精英对城市性的僵硬理解相反，欢迎那些融合民俗文化要素的其他城市性形态，是本书论证的核心。埃尔曼早在1998年就解释说，“随着世界范围内对多样性与族群身份的意识不断增强，一种针对‘谁是城市的、什么是城市的’这一问题的批判性取向正在形成。这有可能使城市居民的定义摆脱共和国精英的垄断”（1998a，542）。埃尔曼对这一问题的精准阐明，与萨森的观察相呼应：“通过主体与环境来界定城市性，并不是自然而然发生的；它往往来自艰辛的努力与痛苦的历程”（2012，85）。这样一条道路必须经过共情。正如理查德·桑内特指出的，“虽然共情一词是现代的，但这种观看行为却是由城市生活的特殊条件所要求的”（1992，233）。在土耳其乡城迁移的漫长历史中，共情在大多数时候都是一种稀缺的美德。
en: The ways migrants become urbanites in the city is a major theme in the seven novels of the corpus, as their analyses in the coming chapters demonstrate. “Change in the traditional culture among migrants seems to occur not as a sudden break with the past, but as a slow assimilation of the urban influence, and also adjustment of the folk culture to it” (40). Welcoming alternative urbanities which incorporate folk culture elements is central to the argument in this book as opposed to the elite’s rigid perception of urbanity. Erman, writing back in 1998, explains that “as the result of the growing consciousness about diversity and ethnic identities in the world, a critical approach to the question of ‘who and what is urban?’ is developing. This has the potential of freeing the definition of an urbanite from the monopoly of the Republican elites” (1998a, 542). This perfect clarification of the issue by Erman resonates with Sassen’s observation that “the definition of urbanity through subject and setting does not simply happen; it frequently comes out of hard work and painful trajectories” (2012, 85). Such a path goes through empathy. As Richard Sennett acknowledges, “though the word

is a modern one, this act of vision is dictated by the peculiar conditions of city life” (1992, 233). In the long history of the rural–urban migration in Turkey, empathy was a scarce virtue most of the time.

zh: 主张对城市的权利
en: Laying Claim to the City

zh: 通过街头贩卖等非正规谋生方式，以及棚屋等非正规住房，迁入者向城市提出了自己的权利主张。阿塞夫·巴亚特将这些策略描述为街头政治的一种形式（2012，119）。巴亚特在一篇文章中试图寻找出路，摆脱新自由主义城市性时代“精英统治与底层者失败”（110）的二分。他强调，左翼将“新自由主义城市［视为］一座失去的城市”：底层者不再期望更好的生活，“城市权利的理想在那里几乎已经消失”（117）。他赞同这些论点的若干方面，同时指出，有必要超越“被动—主动、胜利—失败这类截然分明的二分”，并考察“新自由主义城市可能无意间为底层斗争提供哪些可能性”（119）。他将街道定义为底层者“不可或缺的资产／资本”，他们可以在这里“维持生存，并再生产经济生活与文化生活”；他将这些活动视为街头政治的一种形式（119）：“在便道上摆摊做生意的街头小贩，把生活延伸到人行道上的穷人，占用公共土地的棚户居民，或在街头游行的抗议者，都参与着街头政治”（120）。
en: Through informal ways of occupation such as vending and informal housing such as shanties migrants lay claim to the city. Asef Bayat describes such strategies as a form of street politics (2012, 119). Bayat, in an article where he searches for a way out of the dichotomy between “elite rule and subaltern’s failure” (110) in times of neoliberal urbanity, stresses that the left sees the “neoliberal city [as] a lost city” where subalterns do not hope for better lives and “where the ideal of the right to the city is all but vanished” (117). While agreeing with various aspects of these arguments, Bayat draws attention to the need for surpassing “categorical dichotomies as passive-active, or win-lose” and examines “what possibilities the neo-liberal city may unintentionally furnish for subaltern struggles” (119). He defines streets as “indispensable asset/capital” for subalterns where they can “subsist and reproduce economic as well as cultural life” and regard them as a form of street politics (119): “street vendors who spread their business on the pavements, poor people who extend their lives onto the sidewalks, squatters who take over public lands, or protestors who march in the streets are all involved in street politics” (120).

zh: 巴亚特将他们的策略定义为“蚕食”（120），也称作“普通人的静默蚕食”（2013，80）。他解释说，“穷人通过蚕食、延展、活动与谋生重新占有公共空间，构成了街头政治的一种表达，同时也滋养并强化了政治性的街道。换言之，通过这种蚕食，被剥夺者不断参与围绕城市空间、并在城市空间之中展开的斗争”（2012，120）。迁入者为了在城市中生存而进行的这种静默蚕食，以这样或那样的方式，出现在以下各章分析的几乎所有小说中。通过搭建棚屋以求栖身而蚕食土地的行为，或有关这一经历的记忆，出现在所有这些小说里。沿街贩卖是静默蚕食的另一种形式，它始终是迁入者生活中的重要现象，因为在工作机会稀少的城市，这是一种自谋职业的方式。这两种现象，加上迁入者以合乘出租车（dolmush）形式自行组织的“公共交通”，共同出现在一本研究他们如何蚕食城市的著作标题中：《有合乘出租车、棚屋与街头摊贩的城市》（Dolmuşlu, Gecekondulu, İşportalı Şehir；Tekeli et al. 1976）。
en: Bayat defines their strategies as “encroachment” (120), as well as “quiet encroachment of the ordinary” (2013, 80). He explains that “the reclamation, by the poor people, of public space through encroachment, stretching out, functioning, and subsisting constitutes an expression of street politics, while simultaneously feeding into and accentuating the political street. In other words, through this encroachment, the dispossessed are constantly engaged in struggles in and about the urban space” (2012, 120). This quiet encroachment of migrants in their struggle to survive in the city appears in this or that way in almost all the novels analysed in the following chapters. Encroachment on land by building shanties for shelter, or memories of this experience, appear in all of them. Vending on the streets, which is another form of quiet encroachment, has always been an important phenomenon in the lives of migrants since it is a means of self-employment in the city where job opportunities are scarce. These two phenomena, together with the self-organised ‘public transport’ of migrants in the form of the share taxi (
), appear in the title of a book on their encroachment in the city:

zh: 不过，迁入者的政治并不限于街头政治；他们也参与“我们通常所理解的政治”。卡尔帕特解释说，政治与政治行动在棚户区迁入者的融入／城市化进程中发挥着重要作用（2009，43）。他将“棚户聚居区中的政治组织与行动”描述为“与城市政府和国家政府互动时，迄今最富活力的形式”（43）。迁入者以聚居区改善协会的名义建立组织，以便“保护财产、发展共同体，并向城市当局争取供水、供电和公交服务等基本城市设施”（43）。此外，他们也意识到自己作为选民在选举中的力量，这有助于他们获得上述设施（43）。对他们而言，选择并支持一个政党意义重大，“不仅因为政党是沟通和向当局施压的渠道，也因为它们是融入城市的机制”（43）。卡尔帕特补充说，棚户区迁入者经常因其政治行动而被批评为机会主义者（43）。缪贝杰尔·克赖确实将“庇护主义”描述为迁入者的一项重要生存策略（2007c，185）。在卡尔帕特看来，被冠以迁入者机会主义之名的情况，是他们遭遇“来自警察、城市居民，有时还有新闻界的敌视态度”（2009，43）的必然结果。他们通过“联合起来，迅速发展组织技能，以及对政治精明而务实的看法”，寻找解决自身问题的办法（43—44）。卡尔帕特如此描述迁入者集体行动的能力，以及这种能力与他们融入城市的联系：“他们作为共同体和个人在城市中求生的斗争，最终形成了集体行动的习惯，以及共同体责任感和公民责任感。政治团体与协会也在无意间成为沟通渠道，棚户居民通过这些渠道，逐渐界定自己新的城市身份，并把自己与外部世界联系起来，其基础不仅是传统，也包括理性决策与利益”（44）。正如这一观察所阐明的，参与政治进程，是迁入者城市化不可分割的一部分。
en: That said, migrants’ politics is not limited to street politics; they are also involved in ‘politics as we know it’. Karpat explains that politics and political action have an important function in the integration/urbanisation process of migrants in shanty towns (2009, 43). He describes “political organization and action in the squatter settlements” as “by far the most dynamic form of interaction with city and national governments” (43). Migrants establish organisations under the banner of the Society for Settlement Improvement in order “to protect the property, develop the community, and secure the basic urban facilities such as water, electricity, and bus service from the city authority” (43). Additionally, they are aware of their power as voters in elections, which is instrumental in accessing these facilities (43). For them, choosing a party and supporting it has great importance “not only as channels of communication and pressure on authorities but also as mechanisms for integration into the city” (43). Karpat adds that migrants in shanties are usually criticised for being opportunistic in their political moves (43). Indeed, Mübeccel Kıray describes “clientelism” as an important survival strategy of migrants (2007c, 185). For Karpat, the situation labelled as migrants’ opportunism is an inevitable result of “hostile attitudes on the part of the police, city residents, and occasionally the press” (2009, 43) that they encounter. They seek solutions to their problems by “uniting and rapidly developing organizational skills and a sophisticated, pragmatic view of politics” (43–44). Karpat describes migrants’ capability for collective action and its connection with their integration into the city as follows: “Their struggle for survival as a community and as individuals in the city eventually creates habits of collective action, a sense of communal and civic responsibility. Political groupings and associations became also inadvertently channels of communication through which the squatters gradually define their new urban identity and relate themselves to the outside world, on the basis not only of tradition but also of rational decision and interest” (44). As this observation elucidates, engaging in political processes is integral to migrants’ urbanisation.

zh: 卡尔帕特认为，棚户区迁入者并不具有“浪漫的革命者所揣测和期待的那种对体制的仇恨与厌恶”（44）。因此，他补充说，激进派未能成功动员棚户居民从事“暴力和激进行动”（44）。相反，许克吕·阿斯兰将20世纪70年代描述为激进左翼在棚户区获得支持的时期，并强调，甚至有多个棚户区就是由激进左翼团体建立起来的，以践行他们对住房权利的信念（2004，85）。阿斯兰指出，这类街区约有十二个。此外，左翼在其他不受其控制的棚户区中，也拥有成员与组织（致作者电子邮件，2016年7月2日）。克维尔吉姆·埃尔坦解释说，应被视为“住房运动”的“棚户区运动”，是20世纪70年代在土耳其蓬勃兴起的“城市运动”的一部分（1999，126）。

阿斯兰所描述的经验便属于这一范畴。尽管存在这些经验，但从宏观层面看，卡尔帕特的分析仍然成立：棚户聚居区的主导倾向，更多地指向民主参与，而非激进主义。卡尔帕特强调，“如果满足诉求和参与政治的正常渠道对棚户居民关闭”，激进意识形态“就可能在聚居区中得到接受”（2009，200）。就在这一刻，城中的乡村迁入者发现了一种潜能，而这种潜能是他或她在村庄时所不可能知晓的。用萨森的话说，“城市，尤其是街道，是一个无权者能够创造历史的空间，其方式是在乡村地区无法实现的”（2013，213）。阿斯兰所说的那些街区，就是这种创造历史的良好例子；然而，在伊斯坦布尔，这类经验并不占主导地位。
en: Karpat argues that migrants in shanty towns did not possess “hate and aversion toward the system, as romantic revolutionaries had speculated and hoped for” (44). Consequently, he adds, radicals were not successful in mobilizing shanty dwellers “for violent and radical action” (44). Şükrü Aslan, on the contrary, describes the 1970s as times when the radical left had support in shanty towns and stresses that there were even various shanty towns established by radical left groups as an implementation of their belief in the right to housing (2004, 85). As Aslan acknowledges, the number of such neighbourhoods was around twelve. Additionally, the left had members and organisations in other shanty towns which they did not control (email to author, 2 July 2016). Kıvılcım Ertan explains that the “shanty movements” which should be regarded as “housing movements” were part of the “urban movements” which flourished in Turkey in the 1970s (1999, 126).

The experiences Aslan explains fall into this category. Notwithstanding these experiences, Karpat’s analysis that the dominant tendency in shanty settlements was not towards radicalism as much as it was towards democratic participation is valid on the macro-scale. Karpat emphasises that radical ideologies “can find acceptance in the settlement if the normal channels for demand satisfaction and political participation are closed to squatters” (2009, 200). This is the moment when the rural migrant in the city discovers a potential that would be unknown to him/her back in the village. In Sassen’s words, “the city, and especially the street, is a space where the powerless can make history, in ways they cannot in rural areas” (2013, 213). The neighbourhoods Aslan refers to are good examples of this sort of history making, yet these experiences were not predominant in the case of Istanbul.

zh: 除少数例外之外，进入下文所分析小说的，是静默蚕食，而不是参与式政治与城市运动。这些作品既没有将迁入者通过参与式政治采取直接行动的能力，也没有将他们建立城市社会运动的潜能，作为主题或信息加以表达。换言之，所选作品几乎没有一部强调这样的事实：迁入者作为行动主体，实际上能够在参与式政治与城市运动的框架下争取自己的城市权利，而非仅仅把自己局限于静默蚕食。
en: Apart from a few exceptions, quiet encroachment, rather than participatory politics and urban movements, enter the novels analysed in the following pages. Neither migrants’ capability of taking direct action through participatory politics, nor their potential to build urban social movements, appear as a theme or message in these books. In other words, almost none of the works in the corpus stresses the fact that migrants as agents can actually fight for their right to the city under the umbrella of participatory politics and urban movements instead of simply confining themselves to quiet encroachment.

zh: 女性：“迁移的火车头”
en: Women: “The Locomotive of Migration”

zh: 本章最后一节聚焦迁移的性别维度。在这里，我们应当记住，在土耳其乡村社会，“女性处于男性的控制之下”，“地位与权力都很低”；伊斯兰的影响增强了父权制的力量，也强化了这一状况（Erman 1997，264）。
en: In this final section of the chapter, the focus is on the gender dimension of migration. At this point, we should remember that in Turkish rural society “women are under male control” and “have very low status and power”, a situation enhanced by Islamic influences which have added to the power of patriarchy (Erman 1997, 264).

zh: 正如塔希雷·埃尔曼准确指出的，在大量有关第三世界城市化与迁移的研究中，女性的角色并未获得多少位置（263）。埃尔曼指出，“女性被假定为纯粹被动的迁移者，只是跟随丈夫、父亲或儿子来到城市”；但她补充说，实际上，“女性在迁移中发挥的作用，比主流迁移文献所描绘的要积极得多”（263）。
en: As Tahire Erman aptly observes, women’s roles do not find much place within the considerable amount of research made on third-world urbanisation and migration (263). Erman acknowledges that “women are assumed to be merely passive movers, following their husbands, fathers or sons to the city”, and adds that, in fact, “women play a much more active role in migration than depicted in mainstream migration literature” (263).

zh: 埃尔曼在1997年撰文，批评“大多数有关迁入者的社会学研究，都是以‘户主’为对象进行的，这通常意味着丈夫或父亲”（263）。然而，卡尔帕特早在1968年开展的研究，就没有这一盲点：他在伊斯坦布尔三个棚户区进行的田野调查中，男女受访者的数量大致相同，分别为467名女性与482名男性（5）。根据这项研究的数据，卡尔帕特认为，女性对于迁居伊斯坦布尔普遍持积极感受（130）。他断言，除了更好的生活水平与物质条件，对女性来说，迁移也是摆脱与夫家亲属密切接触的一种方式（131）。然而，与这种对城市生活的积极态度同时存在的，是女性对自己在城市社会等级中所处的低下位置表达出的强烈不满（131）。这很可能与女性比男性更能觉察并表达自身感受有关；这一问题超出了本书范围。卡尔帕特还补充说，“在棚户区（gecekondu）居民中，女性在观念、生活方式与抱负水平上的差异，比男性表现得鲜明得多”（131）。他观察到，棚户区中的女性“希望在选择未来丈夫时拥有发言权，表现出一种非同寻常的独立意识”（153）。他也强调，她们倾向于“嫁给城里的男人，因为城市中的成长经历使他们举止得体，尊重女性”（153）。
en: While Erman, writing in 1997, criticises the fact that “most of the sociological research on migrants has been carried out with ‘the heads of the household,’ which usually means husbands or fathers” (263), Karpat’s research, dating back to 1968, was one which did not have this blind side, and in the fieldwork which he conducted in three shanty towns in Istanbul the number of interviewees were more or less the same: 467 women and 482 men (5). Based on the data of this research Karpat contends that women predominantly had positive feelings for having moved to Istanbul (130). He asserts that in addition to better living standards and physical conditions, for women, migration was also an escape from close contact with in-laws (131). Together with this positive attitude about being in the city, however, women expressed an intense resentment about their inferior position on the social scale in the urban setting (131). This might well be connected with women’s greater capacity for awareness and expression of their feelings than men possess, a subject beyond the scope of this work. Karpat also adds that “the differences of outlook, style of living, and level of aspiration showed much sharper variation among the

[shanty] women than men” (131). He observes that women in the shanty towns demonstrate “an unusual sense of independence in wanting to have a say in the choice of their future husbands” (153). He also underscores their preference “to marry men from the city because of their urban upbringing, which made them well mannered and respectful of women” (153).

zh: 同样，埃尔曼根据自己在土耳其首都安卡拉的迁入女性中开展的田野调查指出，“土耳其迁入女性对城市有着强烈的偏好”（1997，267）。她提到，在土耳其迁移的早期，男人先迁往城市，然后妻子跟随而来；但过了一段时间，“大多数迁入者开始以家庭为单位迁往城市”（264）。根据她在20世纪90年代末进行的研究数据，埃尔曼强调，女性并不总是仅仅跟随丈夫进城；在某些情况下，她们是迁移过程的发起者（268）。她的研究也表明，在一些家庭中，女性比男性更积极地推动家庭在城市安顿下来，运用人际关系与技能来创造收入机会（268）。她总结说，“与村庄中女性为丈夫及其家人付出的艰苦却不被认可的劳动，以及大家庭和村庄共同体对女性、尤其是儿媳的控制相比，土耳其农家女性更愿意生活在城市”（270）。
en: Similarly, Erman, based on her fieldwork among migrant women in Ankara, the capital of Turkey, states that “Turkish migrant women have a strong preference for the city” (1997, 267). During the early era of migration in Turkey, she notes, men migrated to cities first, and then their wives followed them; however, after a while “the majority of migrants started moving to the city as families” (264). Based on the data of her research conducted in the late 1990s, Erman stresses that women were not always simply following their husbands to the city but in some cases were initiating the migration process (268). Her research also reveals that there were cases where the woman of the family was more active than the man in getting the family settled in the city, using connections and skills for creating income opportunities (268). She concludes that “when compared to the hard, unacknowledged labor of women for their husbands and the husbands’ families in the village and the control extended families and the village community have over women, especially over daughters-in-law, city living is preferable for Turkish peasant women” (270).

zh: 在迁入家庭中，外出工作的女性人数相对较少（Kıray 1999，170；Erman 1997，265）。缪贝杰尔·克赖指出，在20世纪50年代的第一波迁移中，迁入女性主要从事家政劳动；此后几十年，她们则在作坊、仓库等地方找到低薪、缺乏保障的工作（1999，170）。在伊斯坦布尔第二代迁入家庭的就业女性中，进工厂做工相当普遍（171）。迁入女性也从事缝纫、编织等家庭生产（171）。克赖强调，以这些方式获得的收入，使家庭中男女之间的力量平衡发生了重大变化（171）。尽管如此，正如克赖所观察到的，“这些工作使迁入女性的劳动报酬远低于应有的水平”（171）。她补充说，迁入女性偏好工厂工作，因为它使人能够拥有家庭以外的生活；第二代女性则希望成为教师或白领，这些是第一代女性连想都不敢想的职业（171）。
en: In the migrant families, the number of women working outside of home is relatively low (Kıray 1999, 170; Erman 1997, 265). Mübeccel Kıray asserts that in the first wave of migration in the 1950s, migrant women predominantly did domestic work while in the following decades they found jobs in low-paid unsecured jobs at places like workshops and warehouses (1999, 170). Among the second-generation migrant working women in Istanbul, employment as factory workers was widespread (171). Migrant women also engaged in domestic production such as sewing and knitting (171). Kıray emphasises that the income made in such ways resulted in serious transformations in the balances between men and women in families (171). Despite that, as Kıray observes, “these jobs keep migrant women’s labour at a rate much lower than it should be” (171). She adds that migrant women favoured factory work, as this presented a life outside of home, and the second-generation women aspired to being teachers or white-collar workers, which first-generation women would never be able to dream of (171).

zh: 在迁移的早期阶段，男性的识字率有所提高，女性却没有；然而，过了一段时间，这种情况发生了变化：在第二代和第三代迁入人口中，女孩在学业上比男孩更为出色（172）。迁入女性支持并激励女儿接受良好的教育，因为这可能带来一份白领工作，以及／或者使她们嫁给从事白领工作或经营小企业的丈夫（172）。克赖认为，即使女性接受教育后并未就业，教育仍然会对她养育子女及与家人互动产生积极影响（173）。1981年，T.申亚珀勒援引一项1976年进行的调查，表示她预期男女棚户居民的识字水平将在短期内趋于相等（1981a，202—203）。她还指出，女孩“教育程度的提高，集中在小学与中学阶段，而不是学院或大学阶段”（203）。
en: During the early phases of migration, the literacy of men but not women increased; however, this changed after a while; in second and third-generation migrant populations, girls became more successful than boys in their studies (172). Migrant women supported and motivated their daughters to get a good education as this could lead the way to a white-collar job and/or marriage with a white-collar or small entrepreneur husband (172). Kıray asserts that even when a woman’s education does not lead to employment it has positive effects on her parenting and interaction with family members (173). In 1981, referring to a survey conducted in 1976, T. Şenyapılı expresses her expectation that the literacy levels of male and female shanty dwellers would be equal in the short term (1981a, 202–203). She also notes that girls’ “increased education is concentrated at the primary and high school levels and not at the college or university level” (203).

zh: 正如埃尔曼所指出的，“在城市生活，通常是以独立核心家庭的形式生活，使女性承担起组织家庭生活的责任，从而提高了她们的自主性。她们被赋予了——出于现实需要——管理城市家庭的更多责任”（1997，270）。克赖把迁入女性的这一角色置于城市中与迁移相关的消费动力框架下加以分析，强调“在城市经济中，迁入者首先是一个消费者。女人是将这一点付诸实践的人”（1999，173）。她认为，“对于迁入家庭来说，‘像城里人一样消费’是成为城里人的首要条件，而女人组织着这种消费”（174）。她解释说，迁入女性把消费分为两类：在第一类中，对于其他人看得见的物品，她实行炫耀性消费；而在第二类中，对于只有家庭成员看得见的物品，她则把消费压到最低限度（174）。她补充说，迁入女性从电视广告中获得大量有关消费品与风格的信息和启发（175）。除了电视之外，正如T.申亚珀勒所观察到的，“用图片讲述浪漫爱情故事的杂志”，也对迁入女性有重要影响（1981a，204）。她将消费定义为，城市社会向居住在棚户区的乡村迁入者“自愿而完整地提供的唯一融入渠道”（206）。她强调，居住在棚屋中的迁入女性，“比丈夫更加在意融入城市生活，因此愿意接受消费刺激和相关消费规范”；所以，她会“推动购置房产、消费品与现代器具，并宽容地对待想要追随城市最新时尚的孩子”（213）。
en: As Erman acknowledges, “living in the city, usually in independent nuclear units, increases women’s autonomy by making them responsible for organizing domestic life. They are given (out of necessity) greater responsibility in administering the urban household” (1997, 270). Kıray analyses this role of migrant women within the framework of consumption dynamics in the city as regards migration, stressing that “in the urban economy the migrant is above all a consumer. The woman is the person who implements this” (1999, 173). She contends that “for the migrant family, ‘consuming like urbanites’ is the first condition of being an urbanite and women organise this” (174). She explains that the migrant woman divides consumption into two categories. In the first category, for products visible to others she practices conspicuous consumption; while in the second category, for the products seen only by the family members she holds the consumption at the lowest minimum (174). She adds that the migrant woman gets a lot of information and inspiration about consumer products and styles from television adverts (175). In addition to television, as T. Şenyapılı observes, “magazines that relate romantic love stories through pictures” are an important influence on migrant women (1981a, 204). She defines consumption as “the only channel for integration offered by the urban society, willingly and completely” to the rural migrants living in the shanty towns (206). She emphasises that the migrant woman living in the shanty “more than her husband, is sensitive to integration into urban life and is therefore open to consumption stimulants and relevant consumption norms” and therefore “pushes for acquisition of real estate, consumer goods, modern gadgets and is tolerant towards children who want to follow the latest urban fashions” (213).

zh: 在城市中，迁入女性在养育子女方面，比留在乡村时拥有更多自由，因为丈夫大多在工作，而老人留在了村里（Kıray 1999，175）。她们也善于建立和维持邻里关系（175）。克赖指出，迁入女性还负责安排与亲属及同乡迁入者之间的社会交往。她补充说，迁入女性会鼓励青春期的女儿适应城市生活；为此，她可能瞒着丈夫和邻居，允许女儿外出，并额外给她零花钱（175—176）。总之，“城中的迁入女性经历着积极的适应过程，并影响着第二代”（177）。
en: In the city, migrant women have more freedom in raising their children than they would do in the countryside as the husbands are mostly at work and the elderly are left behind in the village (Kıray 1999, 175). They are also successful in making and maintaining neighbour relations (175). As Kıray acknowledges, the migrant woman is also in charge of organising social relations with relatives and fellow migrants from the same place of origin. She adds that the migrant woman encourages her adolescent daughter to adapt to city life, with the intention she might give her permission to go out and supply her with extra pocket money secretly from her husband and neighbours (175–176). In conclusion, “the migrant woman in the city goes through an active adaptation process and influences the second generation” (177).

zh: 威尔逊指出，“虽然女性与少数群体、儿童和穷人一样，仍然不是完整意义上的公民，因为她们从未被允许充分而自由地进入街道，但工业生活仍然将她们带入了公共生活；她们在城市的缝隙中生存并蓬勃发展，以自身独特的方式
如上所述，一些迁入女性有幸获得工业岗位，另一些则从事家政服务或家庭生产。无论如何，她们的生活都与留在村庄时截然不同。西蒙·帕克关于这些女性重新占有公共空间的解释——借用威尔逊的话说，即“
”——值得长引如下：
en: As Wilson acknowledges, “although women, along with minorities, children, the poor, are still not full citizens in the sense that they have never been granted full and free access to the streets, industrial life still drew them into public life, and they have survived and flourished in the interstices of the city,
in their own particular way” (1991, 8).

As explained above, some migrant women were fortunate enough to have industrial jobs while others worked as domestic helpers or performed domestic production. In any case, they had a completely different life than they would do back in their villages. Simon Parker’s explanation of these women’s reclaiming of the public space, “negotiating the contradictions of the city” to borrow Wilson’s phrase, is worth quoting at length:

zh: 对于工人阶级女性，或较不富裕阶层的女性而言，街道在更大程度上是一个共同体空间，甚至是一个女性化的空间，因为成年男性要么在工作，要么在酒馆或酒吧这个封闭的世界里享乐。因此，在工作日，公共设施、市场以及街道本身，主要成了女性的领域。所以，在讨论“城市景观的性别化”时，不能想当然地认为它意味着城市空间的“男性化”；还应记住，与男性一样，女性的城市经验也会因其社会身份及族群／文化身份而表现出相当显著的差异。（Parker 2004，144）
en: For working-class women, or women from the less affluent social classes, the street was much more of a communal space, or even a feminised space, to the extent that adult males were either at work or enjoying the closed world of the public house or bar. This left public amenities and markets as well as the street itself as a mostly female domain during the working week. Therefore, it is important when discussing the “gendering of the urban landscape” not to assume that this means “the masculinisation” of city spaces, and to remember that the urban experience varies quite markedly depending on women’s social and ethnic/cultural identity as much as it does for men. (Parker 2004, 144)

zh: 帕克的观察非常适用于伊斯坦布尔的乡村迁入女性：她们为家人购物，步行送孩子上学，与邻居保持活跃的往来，等等。不过，我们不应忽视这一事实：与男性相比，融入和城市化对女性更具挑战性。正如埃尔曼所观察到的，“迁入女性只能以自己的居住环境、亲属和邻居作为自我认同的基础；迁入男性则有自己的职业，有时还会在工作中与原有城市居民互动，并与城市中早已发展起来的部分发生联系，这些都使他们有理由感到自己是城市居民”（1998a，550）。对于拥有正式工作的迁入女性而言，情况会有所不同，但她们只占很小的比例。
en: Parker’s observation is very much valid for the rural migrant women in Istanbul who do the shopping for their family, walk their children to school, have vivid relations with their neighbours, and so forth. That said, we should not overlook the fact that integration and urbanisation is more challenging for women than for men. As Erman observes, “while migrant women do not have anything but their housing environment and their kin and neighbors as the basis for their self-identities, migrant men have their occupations and occasionally inter-actions with the more established urbanites at work, as well as their interactions with the established parts of the city as the basis for feeling themselves to be urbanites” (1998a, 550). The case would be different for migrant women who have formal jobs, but they are only a small minority.

zh: 迁入女性是一个高度异质的群体，其经济、社会、文化、族群和宗教背景各不相同，因而在适应过程、与父权制的斗争，以及最终争取到的自由方面，表现出巨大的差异。在城市中，“有些人在城市提出的苛刻条件与挑战面前变得主动，在家庭中获得了一定的权力和强烈的自我意识；有些人的生活负担较轻，却缺乏那种权力；有些人为家庭辛勤劳作，却仍然缺乏那些主动型女性所享有的权力；还有一些人，则努力挣脱传统的性别角色”（Erman 1998b，159）。城市生活对迁入女性是一场艰难的考验：她们应对着家庭生活中不断变化的角色与责任，努力维系微妙的平衡。女性这些变化中的角色与新责任，是迁移现象的一项重要动力。正如法特玛居尔·贝尔克泰指出的，“在迁移后于城市中求生的过程中，女性成为火车头”（2019，第93分钟）。贝尔克泰强调，“在与贫困和不利处境的斗争中，女性一直以来都更有韧性”（同上）。事实上，迁移带来了翻天覆地的变化，在这一过程中，女性对于维系家庭的完整发挥着巨大的作用。
en: Migrant women constitute a highly heterogeneous category based on economic, social, cultural, ethnic and religious background resulting in tremendous differences in their adaptation processes, struggles with patriarchy and the consequent freedoms they manage to gain. In the city, “some have become ‘initiating’ in the face of the demanding conditions and challenges the city provided and have gained some power and a strong sense of self in the family; some enjoy less demanding lives, yet lack that kind of power; some have worked hard in the family but still lack the power the initiating women enjoy; and still others struggle to break away from traditional gender roles” (Erman 1998b, 159). Life in the city is a difficult test for migrant women: they battle with changing roles and responsibilities within their family life, striving to protect delicate balances. These changing roles and new responsibilities of women is a major dynamic in the migration phenomenon. As Fatmagül Berktay points out, “during survival in the city after migration, women become the locomotive” (2019, min. 93). Berktay stresses that “women are and have been more resilient in the struggle with poverty and disadvantage” (ibid.). Indeed, women have a tremendous role in keeping their family together through the sea change they face upon migration.

zh: 贝尔克泰补充说，“女性对城市权利的诉求，与一切受压迫、受剥削者对城市权利的诉求相呼应”（2019，第22—23分钟）。在下文对七部小说的分析中，我们将通过作品中的女性人物，考察这一事实如何在主题上得到展开，同时探讨有关迁入女性的其他问题。
en: Berktay adds that “women’s demand for the right to the city corresponds to the demand for the right to the city by all those who are oppressed and exploited” (2019, mins. 22–23). In the analysis of the seven novels in the following pages, we will address thematic elaborations of this fact as well as other issues about migrant women through the female characters in the works.

zh: 埃尔坦将土耳其的社会运动分为两大类：（a）20世纪70年代的城市运动：市政运动（以公民社会框架为基础的参与式、民主式市政实践，如伊兹米特与法特萨的经验）；棚户区运动；以及以城市为重点的环境运动（125）。（b）20世纪80年代以来的新社会运动：具有更广泛生态范围与议程的环境运动（126）。
en: Ertan divides the social movements in Turkey into two main groups: (a) the urban movements of the 1970s: municipality movements (participatory and democratic municipalities based on the civil society framework such as the İzmit and Fatsa experiences); shanty movements; and environmental movements with an urban focus (125). (b) New social movements from the 1980s onwards: environmental movements with a wider ecological scope and agenda (126).
